definitions.explanation: Describes something of the smallest possible size, degree, or amount. Used both as a noun and as a modifier with の.

examples.japanese: {極小|きょくしょう}のカメラが{開発|かいはつ}された。
examples.english: An extremely small camera was developed.

examples.japanese: この{部品|ぶひん}は{極小|きょくしょう}サイズで{肉眼|にくがん}では{見|み}えにくい。
examples.english: This component is so tiny that it's hard to see with the naked eye.

examples.japanese: {被害|ひがい}を{極小|きょくしょう}に{抑|おさ}えるための{対策|たいさく}を{講|こう}じた。
examples.english: We took measures to keep the damage to an absolute minimum.

notes:
Can function as a noun meaning "the very smallest" or as a modifier ({極小|きょくしょう}の) meaning "extremely small, minute." In mathematics, {極小|きょくしょう} refers to a local minimum (as opposed to {極大|きょくだい}, local maximum).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {極小|きょくしょう}サイズ — extremely small size
- {極小|きょくしょう}の{粒子|りゅうし} — minute particles
- {被害|ひがい}を{極小|きょくしょう}にする — to minimize damage
- {極小|きょくしょう}{住宅|じゅうたく} — micro-house; tiny dwelling

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {微小|びしょう} — very small, minute (more technical/scientific)
- {最小|さいしょう} — smallest, minimum (superlative; the absolute least)
- {極|ごく}{小|しょう}さい — an emphatic phrasing meaning "extremely tiny"

PRONUNCIATION:
The reading きょくしょう is the standard on'yomi compound. The alternative reading {極小|ごくしょう} also exists and is sometimes used interchangeably, though きょくしょう is more common in formal and technical contexts.
